chapter: First bands, illness and Houston life
title: An only child; his mother's sacrifices
summary: Cobb describes being an only child, his mother boarding him out of her $10 pay, and relieving her once he earned $34.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Arnett, were you an only child?
Only one. Maybe that's why ...and my daughter is the only child. Is that good or bad?
It depends on how you turn out.
Huh?
I say it depends, doesn't it -- what you do with your life, because I mean, sometimes they say an only child is a spoiled child.
Oh, I wasn't spoiled. I tell you what happened.
Your grandfather saw to that.

Yeah, well, that helped me, and I tell you, when I told you I worked at the Harlem Grill for $34 a week, my mother was making $10 -- my purpose of going to work was to help my mother. My mother boarded me out to work, and
out of her ten, she paid seven a week for me. Listen, I want you to hear, but see, she lived in the servants' quarters.
She lived where?
She lived in the servants quarters where she worked.
Oh, I see.

And she come and I'd see her maybe once or twice a week at the most, where she boarded me out. And she would buy my clothes, she kept me neat -- I'm gonna show you a picture in the hall when I was in school, how my mother kept me looking good while I was coming through school, and I didn't know the difference, but she put the best shoes on me, and she had holes in hers, with a newspaper inside there that would wear out, walking, and she'd out another piece of newspaper in there, but she did. That's the kind of mother I had.
Wasn't she -- you were making some money -- what about the $34?
Huh?
I say she's giving you 7 our of her 10 -- what did you do with the 34?
When I said she was paying 7, out of 10, I hadn't started making the $34 yet.
Oh, I see. I see.
But when I started making $34, I relieved her of everything.
Right.

I bought my own clothes, where she was buying them before, and I did it because I knew my mother was doing a beautiful job at what she did, and she couldn't have nothing because of me -- because she wanted me to have the best.
Yes, I follow you.
